themes_detail.label: Street Deterioration Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 133 THIS WEEK, up 363% from the 8-week average of 28.8 weekly complaints (z-score: 10.71), suggesting widespread pavement failure or infrastructure collapse across Astoria/LIC requiring urgent investigation into root cause and city response.
evidence: 133 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 28.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (363% spike, z-score 10.71)
Street Sign - Dangling complaints UP 567% last week (10 complaints vs. 1.5 average, z-score 6.43)
689 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (435 alterations) suggesting ongoing construction activity that may be degrading streets
reporting_angles: Canvass neighborhoods to document which blocks are affected and identify pattern (pothole corridor vs. widespread)
Obtain DOE/DOT records on street repair backlogs and budget allocation to CD 401

themes_detail.label: Encampment Surge in Parks
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 51 THIS WEEK, up 416% from the 8-week average of 9.9 (z-score: 5.71), coinciding with Park Rules violations up 10,300% (13 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 average) and Park Noise up 2,300%, indicating a major homeless presence or encampment crisis in district parks.
evidence: Encampment complaints: 51 THIS WEEK vs. 9.9 weekly average (416% spike, z-score 5.71)
Park Rules violations: 13 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 average (10,300% spike, z-score 38.93—highest severity on dataset)
Park Noise complaints: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 average (2,300% spike, z-score 8.69)
Community Board repeatedly requests 'new homeless shelters or SROs' and 'improve safety at homeless shelters'—pattern of unmet need
reporting_angles: Identify which parks are most affected (likely Astoria Park, LIC Waterfront Park) through 311 data geocoding
Interview parks advocates, DHS officials about shelter capacity and why people may be encamping rather than sheltering
Document conditions: sanitation, public safety incidents, service access

themes_detail.label: Public Urination & Sanitation Spike
themes_detail.summary: Urinating in Public complaints surged to 3 last week, up 1,100% from the 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 6.35), and Unsanitary Pigeon Condition complaints hit 3 THIS WEEK (up 700% from 0.4 average), suggesting acute sanitation and quality-of-life degradation in outdoor spaces.
evidence: Urinating in Public: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (1,100% spike, z-score 6.35)
Unsanitary Pigeon Condition: 3 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 average (700% spike, z-score 5.42)
Spike aligns with encampment surge (51 complaints this week), suggesting homeless population growth in public spaces
reporting_angles: Connect to encampment surge: are public urination complaints concentrated near park encampments or transit hubs?
Interview sanitation workers and BIDs about pigeon/rat population and whether food waste/encampments are attracting pests
Check if NYPD public lewdness enforcement has dropped

themes_detail.label: Street Sign Infrastructure Failure
themes_detail.summary: Dangling Street Sign complaints jumped to 10 last week, up 567% from the 1.5 weekly average (z-score: 6.43), suggesting widespread street furniture failure or lack of maintenance that poses public safety risk and may reflect broader infrastructure neglect.
evidence: Street Sign - Dangling: 10 complaints last week vs. 1.5 weekly average (567% spike, z-score 6.43)
Part of broader street infrastructure crisis (Street Condition up 363% this week)
Indicates deferred maintenance or contractor failure in public realm
reporting_angles: Photograph dangling signs; obtain DOT records on sign maintenance contracts and inspection schedules
Determine if spike correlates with specific DOT contractor or maintenance cycle failure

themes_detail.label: Tree Planting Surge or Environmental Initiative
themes_detail.summary: New Tree Requests spiked to 3 two weeks ago, up 2,300% from the 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 8.69), potentially signaling either resident demand for green space or mobilization around a community tree-planting initiative, but signal is older (2 weeks) and may be isolated incident.
evidence: New Tree Request: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average (2,300% spike, z-score 8.69)
Community Board has requested 'Other capital budget request for DPR' (parks) year after year—possible pent-up demand
One-time spike (only 3 requests); may reflect isolated event rather than sustained trend
reporting_angles: Determine if spike was driven by single community event (e.g., local group requesting trees in park) or organic resident demand
Interview Parks Department on tree-planting budget and queue for CD 401
